column1: # Class relaxation rules for the shapes pipeline (see relaxation/RelaxationRules.kt and
# backend/mat/SHAPES.md "Relaxed classes").
# Format: class.name<TAB>level<TAB>reason (reason is required — say WHICH
# merge the rule unblocks; a rule is a conscious decision to hide something).
# Three levels:
#   class-only                (analyzer) only the class matters; children
#                             concealed from the key, stay in scope
#   set-children              (analyzer) child multiplicities collapse to 1;
#                             on an SCC member it quotients the WHOLE SCC
#                             (WL-color quotient: identical members dedupe),
#                             because an SCC is one strongly-connected object
#                             and member multiplicity is a children-list fact
#   conceal-field:<name>      (extraction) drop this named field of the class
#                             and all subclasses — the edge never enters the
#                             graph; the surgical choice for a lazy/cache
#                             field whose PRESENCE is state
# Rules on abstract classes cover the runtime _Decorated subclasses (exact
# MAT class hierarchy). mat-analyze applies field rules during extraction and
# class rules during analysis in the same JVM.
org.gradle.internal.resource.transport.http.ApacheCommonsHttpClient
column3: With vs without an instantiated InternalHttpClient (cold-cache first resolutions vs warmed) splits per-module resolver chains; the merge is blocked only below this object (verified: run-jfr-38 retained set, SHP1 diffs terminate here)

column1: org.gradle.api.internal.artifacts.repositories.resolver.ExternalResourceResolver
column3: Lazy field (Gradle ExternalResourceResolver.kt:290 create-on-first-use): set only where a real artifact download happened (cold-cache first resolutions), null elsewhere; its presence splits the UserResolverChain SCC. Field-level concealment drops exactly this edge — the AR objects leave the scope; everything else about MavenResolver stays exact. Verified: chain SCCs merge, 181 content groups unchanged (run-jfr-38)

column1: org.gradle.api.internal.artifacts.configurations.DefaultConfiguration
column3: description is UI text, not structure. The six alphabetically-first modules share their configuration description Strings with the IDEA tooling model (sync OOM'd mid-model-build), which cuts those Strings from their retained sets and splits their SCCs (String×5/6 missing). Concealing the field removes the split AND the uniform noise: every module's SCC loses the description edges identically. Verified: the six modules merge into their population groups (run-jfr-38)

column1: com.google.common.cache.LocalCache$LocalManualCache
column3: Guava segment tables/queues initialize lazily on cache writes, so the same cache class splits per instance by initialization depth (12 singleton SCC shapes vs one 38,994-instance shape inside resolver chains on run-jfr-38). A cache is transient infrastructure: concealed from referrers, cached objects stay in scope and keep their counts.

column1: org.gradle.api.internal.artifacts.ivyservice.resolveengine.result.DeduplicatingComponentSelectorSerializer
column3: Traced via a pair diff (run-jfr-38 debugUnitTestRuntimeClasspath :api:f0-api vs :api:f939-api, ndirect 2 vs 3): the single origin divergence was this object's writeIndex HashMap (155+ndirect same-shaped entries, mult 157 vs 158 on the projected table). Per the Gradle source it is a per-serialization-pass dedup index over ComponentSelectors ("should not be reused to serialize multiple graphs") — its fill level records HOW the serialization walk proceeded, not WHAT the configuration contains. Transient infrastructure: concealed from StreamingResolutionResultBuilder; the map, the readIndex list and the delegate stay in scope with exact counts.

column1: org.gradle.api.internal.artifacts.ivyservice.resolveengine.artifact.DefaultVisitedArtifactResults
column3: Resolved dependency-closure contents (including cardinality) are intentionally excluded from configuration shape identity. artifactsById contains one ArtifactSet per visited graph node, so closure sizes split otherwise identical configuration SCCs (the 24-member lint-classpath SCC family: 102 -> 10 shapes; root shapes: 268 -> 81 on run-jfr-38). This is a targeted owner rule, unlike rejected Object[] set-children: resolution objects stay in scope with exact counts, but their contents no longer propagate into referrer keys.

column1: org.gradle.api.internal.artifacts.DefaultResolverResults
column3: DefaultConfiguration.currentResolveState is a second path from configuration SCCs to the resolved graph, resolved configuration and artifact-selection services; concealing DefaultVisitedArtifactResults alone leaves those closure differences in the key. Class-only conceals the cached result while preserving Optional empty/present state and all children/counts. With DefaultSelectedArtifactSet below: 1713 -> 1656 shapes, 81 -> 78 root shapes, no previous root shape splits (run-jfr-38).

column1: org.gradle.api.internal.artifacts.ivyservice.resolveengine.artifact.DefaultSelectedArtifactSet
column3: ResolutionResultProviderBackedSelectedArtifactSet.delegate is the other resolved-content path: exactly isomorphic 46-member configuration SCCs still had different resolved graph results and empty vs five-entry resolved artifact lists. Class-only conceals selection contents while preserving delegate null/present and all children/counts; declared dependencies and registered collection actions still split. Verified with DefaultResolverResults: :classpath 5 -> 4, incomingCatalogForLibs0 2 -> 1, kotlinBuildToolsApiClasspath 3 -> 2 variants (run-jfr-38).

column1: org.gradle.api.internal.artifacts.configurations.DefaultLegacyConfiguration_Decorated
column3: A configuration's strong core (the DefaultLegacyConfiguration+String+DefaultDomainObjectSet+ElementShadow SCC) carries exactly 7 identical members per direct project dependency (416+7*ndirect members, established by per-instance heap inspection in the root-cause analysis), so modules split purely by HOW MANY identical shadow members they have — a children-list fact: ndirect remains visible in the key through the distinct DefaultDependencySet/DefaultPublishArtifactSet members. set-children quotients the SCC (identical members dedupe) and normalizes child multiplicities; distinct declared dependency/artifact-set members still split, while resolved closure contents are excluded by the targeted rule above. Verified: 50/50 population merges preserved, implementation-family roles 12 -> 3 (run-jfr-38).

column1: # REMOVED with prejudice (kept as a record of the reasoning):
#   java.util.HashMap$Node[] set-children — superseded by the traced
#     DeduplicatingComponentSelectorSerializer rule above: the only real
#     count-divergence lived in that serializer's writeIndex; normalizing
#     EVERY HashMap in the heap was a lazy over-broad shortcut.
#   java.lang.Object[] set-children — still rejected as over-broad: its
#     divergence includes DefaultVisitedArtifactResults closure cardinality,
#     but normalizing every array also erases unrelated composition. The
#     deliberate closure exclusion belongs at that owner (the class-only rule
#     above), not on every Object[] in the heap.
